title: Prove: Sliding window moves each pointer at most n times
body:
A sliding window over an array of n elements runs in O(n) time when each pointer only moves forward.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

title: Invariant: Sliding window moves each pointer at most n times
body: At the start of every iteration the half-open interval [left, right) is the current window and right is one past the last inspected element.

title: Proof step: Empty window
body: Set left = right = 0. The window is empty and the invariant holds before any input is consumed.

title: Proof step: Right pointer only advances
body:
Each iteration admits at most one new element by increasing right, so right advances at most n times.

Depends on: init

title: Proof step: Left pointer only advances
body:
Invalid windows are repaired by increasing left; it never decreases, so left also advances at most n times.

Depends on: init

title: Proof step: Sum the pointer moves
body:
At most n expansions plus at most n shrink steps gives O(n) total work, with O(1) extra space.

Depends on: expand, shrink
